extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and PR technicians/managers (planning films, displays, and special events)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for planning, scripting, producing, projecting, distributing PR films and for designing, staffing, and evaluating exhibits, multimedia presentations, open houses, tours, and annual meetings. Emphasizes practical, logistical, and communication-objective criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Film format selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select film format appropriate to intended use and technical requirements (Super-8 vs 16-mm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Super-8 works best where commentary can be provided by a live narrator and for documentation of building sites or one-time special events; small format also suits displays (spliced loops for back-projection). 16-mm is the standard for sound films for television, distribution to schools, and training use: it gives a bright, clear image even in large auditoria, has effective sound systems, is easier for editors to handle/cut, and film labs routinely perform special effects (wipes, dissolves, fades). Choose format based on audience size, need for optical/sound effects, editing/lab services, and projection equipment availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin film planning with a concise synopsis (about 100 words) that summarizes the main point, style, and mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even a major epic should be boiled down to ~100 words to indicate main point and tone; use this as the first approval step before treatment and script.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a treatment: a scene-by-scene (not necessarily shot-by-shot) explanation of everything that will happen in the film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the treatment to visualize the film and to obtain approval prior to scripting; treatments should include sequence of scenes, major actions, and scene intent (example: open with two canoeists driving past a sign to establish location).

rubrics_metrics.name: Script and storyboard completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a full script (camera directions, times, dialogue if appropriate) and a storyboard showing each shot sketch, object relationships, character movement, and camera motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Storyboards help nontechnical top managers visualize the film and should include title cards, credits, still pictures, charts/graphics, and notes on studio lighting/filming requirements. Include camera directions, estimated shot lengths, and any dialogue or timing cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of titles, credits, and graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all title cards, credits, still pictures, charts or graphics in the storyboard and production plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are prepared by the art department or typographer, filmed with studio lighting, and edited into the finished film; consider tints/sepia tone for historical B/W photos to integrate them into color films.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional tie-ins and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan promotion of the film while it is being processed: posters, brochures, fact sheets, and audience-specific materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used in schools, prepare lesson guides, bibliographies, background information, minicourses, discussion guides, and suggested projects. Provide fact sheets at showings because audiences cannot store/retrieve film information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution channel selection matched to target publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose distribution channels that will actually reach the target public, not just maximize general distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include audiovisual distributors (for loans/showing records), educators and clubs (free loans), movie theaters (industrial shorts), cable television, bill-stuffer brochures, minitheaters at public sites (trade exhibitions, fairs, airports, stations). Use employees and organizational networks as distribution advocates. Obtain mailing lists where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure reach against communication objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Track how many members of the target public see the film and avoid equating broad distribution with reaching the target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count viewers and observe whether they belong to the intended target public. Keep records from distributors, theater showings, and sign-in lists to measure effectiveness relative to the communication objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projection/presentation technical checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Control presentation to ensure reliable and aesthetically pleasing projection using a technical checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key items: totally dark room; no viewer seated more than a 30-degree angle from screen center; stable projector support; heavy-duty power cords secured to floor with wide tape; replacement projection lamps and fuses; emergency splices and masking tape; short roll of unimportant film for testing; advance film positioning (first frame of titles) and hold until audience ready; contingency plan (person to ad-lib) for interruptions; rewind/clean/repair/store film in cool dry place immediately after showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning for projection failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a contingency plan and personnel to handle interruptions or malfunctions during projection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign someone (not projectionist) to ad lib for a few minutes to keep audience attention; prepare related topics to talk about rather than duplicating film content; have emergency splices, backup lamps, fuses, and extra tapes on hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective-driven event selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure every exhibit or special event has a clear management-approved objective (communication/message retention, sometimes attitude/behavior change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using techniques because they are enjoyable to staff; choose an objective (often communication and message retention), be realistic about the publics' likely behavior (active vs curious), and weigh time and budget against possible results before approving the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation design for exhibits and events
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate events by counting attendees, assessing whether attendees match target public characteristics, and measuring message retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counting alone is insufficient; observe attendee characteristics, randomly ask attendees about problem recognition or intended behavior, or collect names for follow-up telephone interviews. Post-event mail questionnaires can work if follow-up mailings achieve at least ~50% response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain show rules and space specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Before designing a display, obtain a detailed outline of show rules, available services (including electric power), and exact space dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ascertain whether back/side walls, curtain separators, or only marked floor space are provided; learn hotel/motel/agency-specific limitations early to design appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for single-use vs multiple-use displays
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the display is single-use (built to specific place/message) or multiple-use (adaptable to various spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because durable materials are costly, design multiple-use exhibits to be easily updated and modified; consider portable quick-assembly interlocking panels and modular components (desks, brochure racks, lighting, storage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Display conceptual clarity and engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the overall impression: whether the display communicates a single concept or several, and whether it encourages active involvement or passive viewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may devote ~70% of space to a major theme and 30% to secondary themes; design elements to invite visitors to enter or interact (e.g., greenhouse with walk-through paths) or to create excitement (interactive games, contests). Tone (serious vs fun) and consistent decor (prestige through color/theming) should support the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traffic flow and lighting planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan routes for approaching and passing the exhibit, the booth orientation, staff positioning, and auxiliary lighting to highlight signs and key objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider directionality of aisles, whether to ‘cant’ the display, and aisle widths that affect proximity. Use auxiliary lights and minispots to eliminate shadows and illuminate products or signage; bring spare bulbs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furniture, flooring, and acoustics integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate seating, display surfaces, writing space, and storage into the design and select floor covering to enhance aesthetics and acoustics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use compatible carpet remnants to improve appearance, prestige, and acoustics; fasten carpeting securely with heavy-duty tape matching color; ensure furniture matches style and colors of exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audiovisual and sound control
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan audiovisual elements so recorded sound enhances the display without competing with neighboring booths; provide hoods/panels to contain sound and back-projection shielding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hoods, plywood, fabric, or insulating panels to keep sound contained; plan canopies/hoods for back-projection to shield from overhead lights; check with show coordinators for adequate electrical outlets and power capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing, dress, and conduct policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff and maintain the exhibit properly: adequate personnel, uniform dress or identification, and rules on consumption and material distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have at least two persons on duty (more for sales/demos); attendants should wear blazers/insignia or badges; forbid food/drink consumption by staff unless provided for clients. Establish policy on who receives printed materials, samples, and premiums; arrange daily restocking if display remains for extended periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead-capture and follow-up process
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a plan to collect names of interested visitors and to provide timely follow-up materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sign-up sheets or other methods to put interested visitors on a mailing list and assure them of follow-up shortly after visiting; prepare calling cards, pens, letterhead, envelopes, stamps, and other contact essentials in the booth kit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit first-aid/repair kit
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a minimal first-aid/repair kit on hand for unforeseen situations and repairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested contents: yardstick/tape measure; variety of tapes (heavy-duty strapping, cellophane, plastic for carpet); compressed air can for cleaning; felt-tip pens and blank signboards; calling cards and stationery; coins for phones; supplier list and key phone numbers; string/rope/wire; extension cords; extra bulbs/lamps; batteries/fuses for A/V; dust rag/whisk broom/air freshener; bottle of water, aspirin, cups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia presentation design
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple images and audiovisual formats to engage attention, present complex concepts, and evoke emotion, designing formats that focus attention on specifics while reminding viewers of context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: multiscreen shows with live actors, quad-format slide shows dividing content by quadrant (title, general view, close-ups), synchronized projectors with dissolves to connect film frames to slides. Choose formats that match the event objective (e.g., fundraising kickoff vs technical orientation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety, security, and legal considerations for tours/open houses
rubrics_metrics.description: Address safety and security needs: protective equipment, insurance coverage, physical protections, and protection of proprietary operations; consult unions where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide if guests must wear hard hats, whether company insurance covers visitors, whether tents/trailers are needed for weather protection, and what measures prevent unauthorized observation of secret manufacturing methods. Coordinate with labor unions and legal counsel as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-house/tour timing and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule events so facility is ready, activities are interesting, program length is appropriate, and alternate dates exist for inclement weather or emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing must make the trip worthwhile but not boring; select an alternate date and ensure interesting activities are planned during the visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitations and RSVP management
rubrics_metrics.description: Send invitations about two weeks in advance, invite comprehensively to avoid offense, involve employees/families where possible, and track RSVPs carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one politician/academic/subcontractor is invited, ensure similar classes of persons are all invited. Keep accurate RSVP records to know who and how many will attend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation, parking, and traffic cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide or ensure bus transportation for remote locations, adequate clearly marked parking, and coordinate with local police for traffic direction as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan entrances/exits and parking to handle expected turnout; for large events obtain police cooperation to direct traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comfort, greeting, and visitor orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide restrooms, checkroom, public phones, nursery areas, adequate hosts/hostesses, official greeters, maps, and printed programs to orient visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VIPs should be met by senior representatives; high-ranked officers should appear and participate. Provide maps and printed programs and ensure hosts can guide guests and handle emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts and promotional mementos
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer token gifts or product packages imprinted with company name as gestures of goodwill with lasting promotional value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select mementos appropriate to audience and event tone to reinforce goodwill and brand recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations and press support
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare press kits for media, hire a photographer, send news releases/photos to media that can't attend, set up a press center, and assign PR staff to assist TV crews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide typewriters/telephones in a press center, deliver releases/photos by mail or messenger to nonattending media, and provide special power/interview arrangements for television crews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refreshments appropriate to audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Select refreshments appropriate to the occasion and attendee profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business/press audiences may expect liquor; families prefer cookies and soft drinks; remote or long events may require box lunches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual meeting legal and logistical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with bylaws and state rules to hold an annual meeting for electing directors and approving financial reports; announce in advance and allow stockholder participation (often via proxies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider venue capacity (own auditorium vs rented space), use of closed-circuit television to link rooms, proxy materials and company publications as notice, and sending special invitations to employees, financial community, elected officials, and dignitaries. Many annual meetings combine with plant tours, social hours, or entertainment.
